prospect.name: Nikhil Amin
prospect.location: United Kingdom based — works UK hours and holds most of his money in pounds. On this call he is in a New York hotel for work, holds a US mobile number, and states he is moving to the US within the month.
prospect.occupation: AI consultancy — confirmed from setter notes on the call: 'Kim mentioned that you're working in ai consultancy is that right' / 'yeah yeah'. Desk-bound roughly nine to evening, with international work travel.
prospect.family_status: Has a brother who has spent the past year on a regimented PT programme and is his reference point for what is achievable. His mother is religious, which is why he does not eat beef. No partner or children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Three gym sessions a week at lunchtime — six exercises as three supersets lifting heavy, then cardio burners, then abs, run through twice, split across back/triceps, chest/biceps and lower body — plus padel twice a week or swimming as a substitute. Takes creatine. Also does physiotherapist-prescribed exercises and pranayama breathing in the mornings. Trained well through most of the previous year, barely trained from February to mid-May 2026 due to work, and has been consistent again for the last month. Has never trained with kettlebells; found Trevor on Instagram.
prospect.medical: History of a bad back, which he now describes as 'probably now completely fine'. Torn ankle ligaments from a football injury that he still actively manages with physiotherapy and wears a strap for during dynamic sport — 'it's tender and I work on it with physio... just making sure that I keep the strength there so that it doesn't roll consistently'. Recurrent night-time muscle stiffness roughly once a week to once a fortnight, which he self-attributes to a magnesium deficiency. Long-standing difficulty falling asleep; for the past two weeks has been using a sleep patch containing L-theanine, melatonin, 5-HTP and GABA, which he says has helped both the sleep and the stiffness.

signals: Already fit, disciplined and self-directed — three gym sessions plus two cardio sessions a week, creatine, tracked protein targets, physio work and morning breathwork.
Explicitly good-to-great rather than rescue: 'pretty much treading water. I work out, I'll put on muscle, I'll see growth... I still feel like there's a lot of fat around my body.'
Price landed with no resistance at all — 'That sounds good to me' — and the only friction was moving funds between currencies.

Reads price as a quality signal and has rejected cheaper options on quality grounds: 'I don't want to pay stupid amounts of money for results that are not going to really be seen... you're not giving me anything that's significantly different to what I'm doing now.'
Motivation is identity and proof rather than crisis: 'to have a strong accountability on myself to be able to prove that I can be disciplined and show that there are results.'

goals.text: Strip fat from his torso — chest, stomach and love handles — and finally get lean rather than just adding muscle
Move with flexibility and dynamism instead of the stiffness he gets from a desk job
Fix the low energy and morning lethargy that leak into his work and social life
Prove to himself he can be disciplined and produce visible, significant results
Have a structure to follow instead of researching it alone and defaulting back to what he already knows

pains.text: Treading water for years — puts on muscle and sees growth, but has never been able to strip the fat; 'getting a lean body that has been my issue my whole life'
Cycles on and off — barely trained February to mid-May, went back down in bench weight and had to rebuild from a lower base
Wakes tired and lethargic every morning despite sleeping through the night, and finds it physically hard to fall asleep
Sedentary from nine until the evening behind a desk, with muscle stiffness he associates with it
Under-eating protein badly for his size — around 100g on a good day against a calculated 180g target at 6'4"
Overwhelmed by conflicting information and ends up reverting to what he already does — 'there's so much out there that you can read about and learn about, and it's kind of overwhelming'
Ankle ligament tear still requiring physiotherapy and a strap for dynamic sport, plus a history of back trouble

objections.rep_response: Asked how much time he needed, accepted 'till the end of the day', and moved the completion to a 9am call the next morning rather than trying to take a partial payment or a card on the call. Did not isolate, and did not explore whether any funds were accessible immediately.

objections.raw_quote: It's just I also was thinking just now that it'd be good. Is it not possible if I can meet Trevor before I pay?
objections.rep_response: Refused the request outright — 'So the process is that it's always after after payment. Why would you ask?' — then argued calendar scarcity, then ran credibility (six years, over 1,000 clients, a guarantee on paper), and finally substituted a one-month 'love it or leave it' at $1,200 instead of granting the meeting.

objections.raw_quote: No, you know, you see things on Instagram all the time, right? And it's like paying without trying. So it's obviously, that's just a standard way that I'd like to…
objections.rep_response: Answered with absolute claims about the guarantee — 'it is virtually impossible for you not to hit your goals' and 'There's no one in the space giving you a guarantee on the results' — then offered the paid trial month, which the prospect accepted.

tiers.note: 'Love it or leave it' trial month with a stated $4,800 top-up to complete the six months

offer.payment_plan_terms: $1,200 for the first month, then $4,800 to top up to the full six months if he continues — 'you only need to top up the remaining 4,800 when you decide at the end of the month that, yeah, you want to follow.' Agreed verbally; nothing paid on the call.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: He's giving you a guarantee, which is on paper, because you're going to be signing also an agreement. ... you will add at least eight kilos to your initial kettlebell on each of the, of the core moves. ... And the guarantee is, if you don't do that, if you won't hit those extra eight kilos, he will work for you for free until you do.

prospect_financials.note: No figures asked for or given, and none of the scripted financial-picture questions ran. The constraint disclosed was currency and settlement timing, not capacity: 'my money is in both places, because it's in dollars, right? ... Mainly my money's in pounds, so I have to, let me sort something out.'

evidence: Verbal agreement to move forward on the $1,200 trial month: 'Okay. That's fine. Yeah. If I can do that, that'd be great.'
Payment link sent in the Zoom chat: 'i'll send you in the zoom chat the the payment link so we can get you in', and the prospect responded to it — 'Oh, you need me to pay now?'
Clean verbal yes to the $6,000 before any objection: 'the investment is 6K and that's it' / 'That sounds good to me' / 'Ready to rock and roll?' 'Ready to change?'
Commitment secured before price: 'are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that 2.0 version of Nikhil?' / 'For sure, for sure.'
Trevor onboarding call booked, US phone number taken and the invite confirmed received: 'Okay, you should get an invite for the meeting. Yeah. Yeah, you got that.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, and it is substantial: nothing was paid. He deferred payment twice — first to end of day, then to a 9am call the following morning — and the transcript ends before any money moves. He also could not confirm receipt of earlier links ('the links haven't been working'), so it is not certain the payment link reached him. The disposition rests entirely on the client-agreed verbal-plus-link rule, not on a collection.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: what he agreed to is a $1,200 trial month explicitly framed as reversible — 'after a month, it's up to you to decide whether you want to continue' — not the $6,000 programme he had verbally accepted ten minutes earlier.
outcome.cash_collection_basis: No cash collected on the call. The agreed first payment is $1,200 under the 'love it or leave it' structure, with $4,800 stated as the top-up to complete six months. Recorded as zero because payment was deferred to a following-day call and nothing in the transcript confirms it.
outcome.next_step: Reconnect 30 June at 09:00 New York time to complete the $1,200 payment once funds have been moved from GBP. Trevor onboarding call already booked for 15:15 the same day, before any payment has landed.

notable.note: The best-run discovery in this batch by a distance — sleep, injuries, training history, plateau, deep why and a genuine two-to-five-year consequence frame all landed, and the commitment check ran before the price. It then unravelled at the close. The prospect asked to meet the coach before spending $6,000 and was refused with 'the process is that it's always after payment. Why would you ask?'; the rep answered a trust request by inventing a price, dropping to a $1,200 trial month with a $4,800 top-up ten minutes after telling him it was a 'one-time cost, no additional fees whatsoever'. No payment was taken, yet Trevor's onboarding call was booked anyway — 'So I'm booking the call with Trevor either way' — which is the exact scenario the manager prohibited on 06/22. Separately, this prospect is an active physiotherapy patient with torn ankle ligaments and a history of back trouble, and nobody asked whether his physio had cleared loaded ballistic kettlebell work.

quality.notes: Sustained label inversion throughout. Whole answers by the prospect carry the rep's label and vice versa — the long nutrition and body-composition passage from roughly 00:13:12 to 00:16:12 runs almost entirely under the wrong name, and the price reveal and 'ready to rock and roll' exchange at 00:45:07 is transposed. Role read from content throughout. There is also a genuine connection dropout between 00:36:47 and 00:38:07 — 'I think my wi-fi went on strike or something' — so roughly eighty seconds of the nutrition pillar is missing from the record.
